purpose: convert geography-independent island polygons into defensible ecological island-system search units before literature review

geographic_master.known_limitation: islands below 20 km2 require a separate small-island supplement

system_unit_rules: Do not treat one polygon as one independent ecological replicate by default.
Use a named archipelago or biogeographically coherent island group as the default system unit when islands share colonization history and are routinely analysed together.
Retain a large nested island as its own system when source-native studies analyse it independently or when it represents a distinct biogeographic or interaction regime.
Do not merge islands solely because they share a country or political administration.
Do not split one research transition into pseudo-independent island systems merely because several polygons were sampled.
Record nested coverage explicitly so broad archipelago searches and island-specific searches can coexist without double counting.
Keep continental-island controls and oceanic islands as different geography classes rather than excluding one class based on expected outcome.
No system is promoted to manuscript evidence merely because a relevant source exists; source admission and manuscript-value promotion remain separate stages.
deduplication_rule: Counts used for world-confrontation breadth must be system-level exact geographic labels after nested overlap review, never raw polygon count.
inference_rule: The 4663-polygon master is a coverage frame only. It is never a validation denominator, prevalence sample, or set of independent tests.
izu_rule: Izu remains outside master-gap promotion until the world-confrontation search stops adding materially new response, process, or falsification states.
